items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: I went on the road with Jimmy Cavallo and we were playing weeklong engagements.

ctx.x: No. I went on the road. Well I’ll explain that one okay. I graduate from high school. I was accepted — I wanted to get to Potsdam because Prof’s family was up there. But once again the physical attraction I had to the female I was going with in high school probably cost me commendable grades. So I got a letter from Prof Stanley that said, he said, “you are head and shoulders above any of the drummers up here but we can’t let you in © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

because your grades are not high enough.” I got out of high school with band, orchestra, chorus and theory. I mean I just barely got out. I couldn’t wait to get out anyway. Then I got accepted to Ithaca College, because I had studied with Warren Benson back when I was at St. Mary’s, with no band director there. And I had paid my $200 initiation fee and I had a jam session with a bass player, now deceased, named Tony Leonardi, and Frank Pezzullo and a whole bunch of guys from the Syracuse area.
